title_en: How an Discretionary Ag Trader "Reads the Soybean Leaves" with Stephen Davis
title_zh: 主观农产品交易员如何“读懂大豆叶”：对话 Davis Commodities 的 Stephen Davis
subtitle_zh: Memphis 老牌主观农产品交易员 Stephen Davis 谈玉米大豆供需、天气、China 需求与风险管理。
summary_zh: 本期 The Derivative 由 Jeff Malec 主持，对话 Davis Commodities 的 Stephen Davis——一位扎根 Memphis 商品圈、做主观农产品交易超过 20 年的老牌交易员。节目从 Memphis 作为与 Chicago、New York 并列的商品交易重镇讲起，回顾 Allenburg、Hohenburg、Dunnevent 三大棉花公司及 Cook grain、Sparks Commodities 的 Willard Sparks 等历史，以及 Davis 如何经由父亲与 Willard 的一通电话入行、后被 John Dickon 的农业 CTA（巅峰管理略超十亿美元、主做玉米大豆小麦与牛）雇用。核心是他的主观基本面方法：同时在供给侧与需求侧向外预测，为每种商品构建供需平衡表，交易周期最短一个月、最长可达数年。他给出两条鲜明纪律——天气只看 15 天为硬性上限，一旦天气变化就拉'开伞索'调整；以及用 delta 精细管理仓位，把因行情快速移动而偏离的目标敞口拉回。他还谈到中国需求、巴西供给、El Nino，以及从农业衍生出的 Plutus 宏观项目。是一堂农产品主观交易的实务课。

turns.en: Welcome to The Derivative by RCM Alternatives. Send it. Hello there. Welcome back to The Derivative brought to you by RCM Alternatives where I think there's nothing to plug today.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 RCM Alternatives 带来的 The Derivative。Send it。大家好，欢迎回到 The Derivative，由 RCM Alternatives 赞助播出，今天好像没什么要宣传的。

turns.en: Plain old RCM and all the cool ways we help investors and managers. Okay, on to this episode where we got to talk with Steven Davis of, wait for it, Davis Commodities.
turns.zh: 就是老牌的 RCM，以及我们帮助投资者和管理人的各种靠谱办法。好，进入今天这期，我们要和 Steven Davis 聊聊——等一下——Davis Commodities 的 Stephen Davis。

turns.en: Steven's been part of the Memphis Commodity scene since he was a teen. He's been trading discretionary ag for clients for over 20 years so we get into how he looks at corn, why soybeans are so much more than edamame, what's the demand from China look like, the supply from Brazil, El Nino and all the rest on the ag markets.
turns.zh: Stephen 从十几岁起就是 Memphis 商品圈的一员，为客户做主观农产品交易已经超过 20 年。所以我们会聊他怎么看玉米、为什么大豆远不只是毛豆、中国的需求什么样、巴西的供给、El Nino 等等农产品市场的话题。

turns.en: We're finding out, send it. All right, we're here with Steven. Steven, how are you? I'm doing great, Jeff. How are you? I'm good. Where on that big world map are you?
turns.zh: 我们这就来听听，send it。好，我们现在和 Stephen 在一起。Stephen，你好吗？我很好，Jeff，你呢？我不错。你现在在那个大大的世界地图上的哪儿啊？

turns.en: You can point it out. All the way over there. So it's not really in the background here. You're in the middle of, oh yeah, that's the middle of Africa.
turns.zh: 你可以指一下。就在那边。所以它其实不在你背景里。你在中间，哦对，那是非洲中部。

turns.en: Yes, no, a little bit further west than that. Where are you for real? You're down in Memphis? I'm in Memphis, Tennessee. Love it. You lived there a long time?
turns.zh: 对，不，比那还要再往西一点。你到底在哪儿？你是在 Memphis 吗？我在 Tennessee 州的 Memphis。真好。你在那儿住很久了吗？

turns.en: I've been here since I was seven. So yes, 47 years. Yeah. Give us a little background on like the, what do they call it? The Memphis Cotton Mafia or the commodity, right?
turns.zh: 我七岁起就在这儿了，所以是的，47 年了。嗯。给我们讲讲背景，他们怎么叫它来着？Memphis Cotton Mafia（Memphis 棉花帮），或者商品圈，对吧？

turns.en: Like a ton of commodity traders and big commodity stuff out of Memphis that I think most people don't know about if they're not deep in this world.
turns.zh: Memphis 出了大量商品交易员和大宗商品的大家伙，我觉得不深入这个圈子的人大多不知道。

turns.en: So the three biggest cotton companies were historically based out of Memphis. You had Allenburg, Hohenburg and Dunnevent. Those have all been since acquired by the bigs, but they were independent.
turns.zh: 历史上最大的三家棉花公司都扎根在 Memphis。你有 Allenburg、Hohenburg 和 Dunnevent。它们后来都被那些巨头收购了，但当初都是独立公司。

turns.en: Another thing that put kind of Memphis on the map was going back to the 70s and cooked grain and cooked grain made a big push into, they started out in cotton and pushed into corn, soybeans in a big way.
turns.zh: 另一件让 Memphis 出圈的事，要回到 70 年代的 Cook grain，Cook grain 大力扩张——他们起步于棉花，然后大举进军玉米、大豆。

turns.en: And that was run in the end by Willard Sparks of Sparks Commodities fame. And out of that as well, Refco, if you remember Refco, I mean, I'm really turning the historical dial back here.
turns.zh: 最后是由 Sparks Commodities 那个大名鼎鼎的 Willard Sparks 掌舵。由此还走出了 Refco，如果你记得 Refco 的话——我可是把历史的指针往回拨了不少。

turns.en: Down in Memphis, you just calm Willard. If you just said Willard, everyone knows who you're talking about, right? Yeah, 100%. 100%. But you also had Charlie McVane and McVane trading is still down here.
turns.zh: 在 Memphis，你就叫他 Willard 就行。你只要说 Willard，人人都知道你说的是谁，对吧？是的，百分之百。百分之百。但你还有 Charlie McVane，McVane trading 现在还在我们这儿。

turns.en: So, I mean, when I got into business in 94, you had Chicago, New York and then Memphis for commodity trading in the United States. Right. Yes.
turns.zh: 所以，我是说，我 94 年入行的时候，美国做商品交易就是 Chicago、New York，然后就是 Memphis。对。是的。

turns.en: Part of me thinks Memphis would have almost been better, but I guess you had all the grains coming from as far as the Dakotas and Minnesota and stuff to get stuff into Chicago.
turns.zh: 我心里有一部分觉得 Memphis 本来几乎会更好，但我想是因为谷物从 Dakotas、Minnesota 那么远的地方运过来，都得进 Chicago。

turns.en: But Memphis seems like a more natural geological hub for all this with the river and everything. Yes. I mean, right here on the Mississippi River, absolutely.
turns.zh: 但 Memphis 有河流什么的，看起来是更天然的地理枢纽。是的。我是说，就在 Mississippi 河边上，绝对的。

turns.en: You know, we see a lot of grain go past us on a daily basis. And then you, as a little seven-year-old, were you just staring at cotton saying, I'm going to trade one day?
turns.zh: 你知道吗，我们每天都能看到大量谷物从我们面前经过。那你呢，作为一个七岁的小孩，你当时是不是就盯着棉花看，心想我总有一天要做交易？

turns.en: Or what was the... How'd you get from there to here? That's kind of funny. No, I grew up in the city, so I had really no idea what I got into business, actually what a soybean looked like.
turns.zh: 还是说……你怎么从那儿走到今天这一步的？这还挺有意思的。不是，我是在城里长大的，所以我入行的时候其实根本不知道大豆长什么样。

turns.en: I'd seen cotton, but you know, if you're not versed in agriculture at all, you know, when you see a soybean field in the cotton field, before you start getting bowls on the cotton, you really don't know which one's which.
turns.zh: 我见过棉花，但你知道，如果你对农业一窍不通，当你看到一片大豆田和一片棉花田，在棉花开始结铃之前，你真的分不清哪个是哪个。

turns.en: So no, it wasn't until after I'd been in the business for a couple of years before I really figured out, okay, this is soybeans, this is cotton.
turns.zh: 所以不是，直到我入行好几年之后才真正搞明白，好，这是大豆，这是棉花。

turns.en: You know, obviously corn is pretty easy to pick out. But also, you know, then you go into the differentials of sweet corn, which we eat versus feed corn, which is obviously fed to animals.
turns.zh: 你知道，显然玉米很容易认出来。但接下来你还要区分我们吃的甜玉米（sweet corn）和显然是喂动物的饲用玉米（feed corn）。

turns.en: Learning how to differentiate those was a little learning experience as well. What did you go to school for this business or something else?
turns.zh: 学会区分这些也是一段小小的学习经历。你上学是学的这个专业，还是别的？

turns.en: So I started out getting my degree in finance at the University of Tennessee in 1990 and my dad... I'm a Gator fan. We got to hang up now. Both of my parents went to the University of Florida.
turns.zh: 我一开始是在 University of Tennessee 读金融学位，1990 年，然后我爸……我是 Gator 球迷。我们得挂电话了。我父母都上的 University of Florida。

turns.en: Of course, you know, my kids hate me because they went to the University of Alabama, my older two, and then my youngest is at Ole Miss. So, you know, Alabama, Alabama, Tennessee is really oil and water.
turns.zh: 当然，你知道，我孩子们恨我，因为他们上的是 University of Alabama，我大的两个，然后最小的在 Ole Miss。所以你知道，Alabama、Alabama、Tennessee 真的是水火不容。

turns.en: Yeah. Ole Miss, not so much. But my daughter looked at me and she said, I'm not wearing that gaudy orange, dad. You got the SEC covered, yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。Ole Miss 还好。但我女儿看着我说，我才不穿那种俗气的橙色呢，爸。你把 SEC 都占全了，是的。

turns.en: Yes, we do. Yes, we do. But my dad did some business with Willard Sparks and I had been doing internships at banks, regional bank here in Memphis and they offered me a third internship and I walked into my dad's office one day and I said, dad, this isn't what I want to do with the rest of my life.
turns.zh: 是的，我们占了。是的，我们占了。但我爸和 Willard Sparks 有些生意往来，我一直在银行实习，就在 Memphis 本地的一家区域银行，他们给了我第三个实习机会，有一天我走进我爸的办公室说，爸，这不是我想做一辈子的事。

turns.en: Yeah. What's a third internship? Like we're going to pay you peanuts or nothing for a third season? Third summer? They were paying me. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。什么叫第三个实习？就像我们要给你第三个夏天付一点点钱或者干脆不付钱？第三个夏天？他们有付我钱。是的。

turns.en: But you know, yeah. It was okay. But it just wasn't what I wanted to do with the rest of my life. And fortuitously, Willard called at that time when I was sitting in his office and my dad said to him, you know, Willard, my son Stephen's here.
turns.zh: 但你知道，是啊。还行吧。只是那不是我想做一辈子的事。碰巧的是，我当时正坐在他办公室里，Willard 打来电话，我爸对他说，你知道，Willard，我儿子 Stephen 在这儿。

turns.en: Yeah. Willard called your dad while you were sitting in his office? Yes. Wow. So my dad, he started out in the Air Force, went into air traffic control, got fired with everybody else by Reagan and eventually moved into private aircraft sales.
turns.zh: 是啊。你坐在你爸办公室里的时候 Willard 给你爸打电话？是的。哇。所以我爸，他最早在空军，后来做空中交通管制，跟所有人一起被 Reagan 给炒了，最后转做私人飞机销售。

turns.en: And so he sold Willard's planes. So that's how my dad got to know Willard. Planes with an S. Well, I mean, it was one at a time, but it was like every time the plane came out of warranty, he'd buy a new one.
turns.zh: 所以他卖 Willard 的飞机。我爸就是这么认识 Willard 的。飞机还是复数。我是说，一次是一架，但就像每次飞机出保修期，他就买一架新的。

turns.en: So it worked out really well for my family. Anyway, my dad said, yeah, Stephen's here and he really doesn't want to do banking again. Is there anybody, you know, he can talk to?
turns.zh: 所以这对我们家有好处。总之，我爸说，是啊，Stephen 在这儿，他真的不想再做银行了。有没有他可以聊聊的人？

turns.en: And Willard said, well, I'll just send him up to Chicago. He can be a runner at the board of trade for me. Perfect. So that was my first introduction to commodities.
turns.zh: Willard 说，那我就把他送到 Chicago 去。他可以给我在 board of trade 当个跑腿的（runner）。太好了。这就是我第一次接触商品。

turns.en: Prior to that, I really had no inkling as to what was going on. So it gets to the floor day one. And by the time the opening bell sounded, I knew I was home.
turns.zh: 在那之前，我真的完全不知道这是怎么回事。所以我第一天到了场内。等到开盘铃响的时候，我就知道我到家了。

turns.en: This is what I want to do with the rest of my life. I mean, it was inject this right into my veins I'm in. So I went back to college. What floor were you?
turns.zh: 这就是我想做一辈子的事。我是说，就像把这个直接注进我血管里，我入行了。所以我回去上大学。你在哪个场内？

turns.en: Board trade. The grain floor. Grain floor. I was on the bond floor for the big 730 reports. And I did spend a little bit of time over at the Merck in the meat pits and helped out a little bit in the S&P 500 pit once again, just as a runner, I mean, knew nothing.
turns.zh: Board of trade。谷物场内。谷物场内。大的 730 报告的时候我在债券场内。我确实也在 Merck 那边的肉类交易坑里待过一点时间，还在 S&P 500 的坑里帮过点忙，同样只是当跑腿的，我是说什么都不懂。

turns.en: Were you like coming from a sleepy bank to the trading floor? You're like, whoa. I was part of you like, what the hell's happening here? That's a hundred percent right, Jeff.
turns.zh: 你是不是那种从一家慢悠悠的银行来到交易场内，然后，哇。你的一部分是不是在想，这到底在发生什么？百分之百没错，Jeff。

turns.en: I mean, you're just sitting there and you're running through numbers on a daily basis as far as looking through balance sheets and trying to help with loan approval and things like that.
turns.zh: 我是说，你就坐在那儿，每天过一遍数字，看资产负债表，帮着做贷款审批之类的。

turns.en: And yeah, that just wasn't really my speed. I still spend a whole lot of time on balance sheets, but they're just different. But anyway, so yeah, it was kind of funny when I was in Chicago.
turns.zh: 是啊，那真的不是我的节奏。我现在还是花很多时间在资产负债表上，只是它们不一样了。总之，是啊，我在 Chicago 的时候有件挺有意思的事。

turns.en: I was looking for more hours because, you know, internships, they really don't pay a whole lot. And the lady who was the assistant to Tom Dittmer, who was the chairman of the board of REFCO, she said, if you want more hours, come and see me.
turns.zh: 我想找更多工时，因为你知道，实习真的赚不了多少。那位当 Tom Dittmer 助理的女士——Tom Dittmer 是 REFCO 的董事会主席——她说，如果你想多干点活，来找我。

turns.en: And I was like, yeah, I need more money. Here I am. So I came up and saw her and she was really impressed with the work that I did and asked me to leave the floor to work directly up in the executive offices.
turns.zh: 我就想，是啊，我需要多赚点钱。我来了。所以我上去找她，她对我做的工作印象深刻，让我离开场内，直接到高层办公室里工作。

turns.en: At the time, REFCO had bought a Russian business publication called Comersant, which is actually still around today, but they had bought the rights to market it outside of Russia and they needed it all digitized.
turns.zh: 当时 REFCO 收购了一家叫 Comersant 的俄罗斯商业刊物，其实它今天还在，但他们买下了在俄罗斯以外发行它的权利，需要把它全部数字化。

turns.en: And so I spent weeks, just weeks going through and this is back in the early days, you know, the old 486 chip and the first optical character recognition software that was out there.
turns.zh: 所以我花了好几周，好几周去处理——这还是早期，你知道，老的 486 芯片和最早的那批光学字符识别（OCR）软件。

turns.en: It was really clunky. So I spent hours and hours just digitizing the old back issues of Comersant. And it was funny because this was the first computer that at least the one that I was aware of, that you could actually do voice commands for macros.
turns.zh: 它真的很笨拙。所以我花了无数小时把 Comersant 的旧期刊数字化。有意思的是，这是第一台——至少我知道的第一台——可以用语音指令来运行宏（macro）的电脑。

turns.en: So I'm sitting here working in back in the day, it was word perfect. I made a bunch of macros where I just had to talk to the computer and it would run the macro and Tom Dittmer walks by my office.
turns.zh: 所以我坐在这儿工作，那会儿用的还是 WordPerfect。我做了一堆宏，我只要对电脑说话，它就会运行那个宏，然后 Tom Dittmer 走过我的办公室。

turns.en: And if you knew Tom, if he wasn't cursing at you, you didn't mean anything. So he curses at me, what are you doing? And I told him what I was doing and he immediately calls the head of operations down into my office.
turns.zh: 如果你认识 Tom，他要是没冲你骂脏话，说明你无关紧要。所以他冲我骂，你在干什么？我告诉他我在干什么，他立刻把运营主管叫到我办公室来。

turns.en: And this is before, you know, electronic order entry was anything, it was off phone. And yeah, he said, show him what you're doing. And I showed him and he said, you're telling me we can't get an electronic order entry system and this guy can sit here and talk to his computer.
turns.zh: 这还是电子下单存在之前的事，当时都是靠电话。是啊，他说，把你做的展示给他看。我展示了，他说，你是告诉我我们搞不到一套电子下单系统，而这小子却能坐在这儿对着他的电脑说话。

turns.en: One of you is wrong. So anyway, that's kind of a funny story. Were you speaking Russian? Did you have to translate or is it already translated?
turns.zh: 你们俩有一个是错的。总之，这是个挺好玩的故事。你说俄语吗？你得翻译吗，还是已经翻译好了？

turns.en: No, it was already translated into English. Yes. Yes. But that was all covering like Ukraine grains? It was covering everything business coming out of Russia at the time.
turns.zh: 不，已经翻译成英文了。是的。是的。但那都是讲 Ukraine 谷物之类的吗？它讲的是当时从俄罗斯出来的所有商业新闻。

turns.en: And back then, back then, I mean, you know, the news out of Russia was, was pretty scarce. Yeah. You know, back in the, what time frame are you talking?
turns.zh: 而且那时候，那时候，我是说，你知道，从俄罗斯出来的新闻相当稀缺。是啊。你知道，回到那个，你说的是什么时间段？

turns.en: 1993. Got it. So pre-internet, pre-everything. So. Right around Rocky 4. Exactly right. I used to tell people like, oh, you want to trade online with air quotes?
turns.zh: 1993 年。明白了。所以是互联网之前，什么都之前。差不多就是 Rocky 4 那阵子。完全正确。我以前跟人讲，哦，你想在网上交易——带引号的那种？

turns.en: I was like, come down, I'd take them to the floor and it was probably Revko where there's like the dot matrix printer printing off the online air quotes again order and they'd just be there to stack them like six inches tall and be like, there's your online order like 17 deep.
turns.zh: 我就说，来吧，我带他们去场内，那大概是在 Refco，有一台点阵打印机在那儿打印出所谓的“网上”订单，他们就把这些单子堆成六英寸高，说，这就是你的网上订单，堆了 17 层深。

turns.en: And when that guy sitting there like silk and the lollipop gets it to it and tears it off, then it's going to get filled. Yes. So yeah. I fought against them for a long time.
turns.zh: 等到那个坐在那儿、含着棒棒糖的家伙把它拿到手、撕下来的时候，它才会被成交。是的。所以 yeah。我抵制电子交易抵制了很久。

turns.en: Like online is not online. It just means you're, instead of using the phone, you're getting it to that desk on the floor in a different way.
turns.zh: 就像“网上”根本不是网上。它只是意味着，你不用电话，而是用另一种方式把订单送到场内那张桌子上。

turns.en: Absolutely. But we got there. Well, anyway, after 93, I went back to college and I talked to the dean of the finance department and I said, this is what I'm going to do with the rest of my life.
turns.zh: 绝对的。但我们最终还是走到了那一步。总之，93 年之后，我回去上大学，我跟金融系的系主任说，这就是我要做一辈子的事。

turns.en: I'd like to take some ad econ classes and I'd like to petition them into my major and they allowed me to do that. So I started learning about futures and options and everything else.
turns.zh: 我想修一些农业经济（ag econ）的课，我想申请把它们算进我的专业，他们同意了。所以我开始学习期货、期权和其他所有东西。

turns.en: And did they have any idea of what was good? Was there actual classes and studies you could do there around? Oh, yes. Yes. University of Tennessee has a pretty decent ag econ department.
turns.zh: 他们知道什么是好的吗？那儿真的有相关的课程和研究可以做吗？哦，有的。是的。University of Tennessee 有一个相当不错的农业经济系。

turns.en: It's nothing like, you know, Mississippi State is really well known in the SEC for their ag econ department, but you know, Tennessee has, they have a good one.
turns.zh: 它比不上，你知道，Mississippi State 在 SEC 里以农业经济系闻名，但你知道，Tennessee 也有一个不错的。

turns.en: I wouldn't call it, it's not on a level of Mississippi State, but at least it got my foot in the door as to understanding futures, understanding options, understanding agriculture.
turns.zh: 我不会说它跟 Mississippi State 一个水平，但至少让我入了门，理解期货、理解期权、理解农业。

turns.en: And it was obviously really helpful as when I graduated, I was offered a job on the brokerage side at Willard Sparks division of Refco in Memphis office.
turns.zh: 而且显然非常有用，因为我毕业的时候，就得到了 Memphis 办公室里 Willard Sparks 那个 Refco 分部经纪业务的一份工作。

turns.en: Memphis. Then you're like, I guess I'm not leaving. Nope. I was home. How long did it take you to say like, okay, I'm going to go do my own, my own thing?
turns.zh: Memphis。那你想，我猜我是走不掉了。不。我到家了。你花了多久才说，好，我要去干我自己的事？

turns.en: Well, I was a broker for 12 years and I knew that wasn't what I wanted to do long time. And then I got hired by a CTA named Dickon Commodities.
turns.zh: 嗯，我做了 12 年经纪人，我早就知道那不是我想长期做的事。然后我被一家叫 Dickon Commodities 的 CTA 雇了。

turns.en: John Dickon ended up being, as far as I know, the largest agricultural CTA in the United States for sure and probably the world at his PQ is managing a little over a billion dollars in basically trading corn, soybeans, soybean products, wheat and cattle.
turns.zh: John Dickon 最后成了——据我所知——美国最大的农业 CTA，肯定是，可能也是世界最大的，在他的巅峰期管理着略超十亿美元，基本上就是交易玉米、大豆、大豆产品、小麦和牛。

turns.en: It's hard to do. It was like turning the Titanic. Yeah, exactly. And when you were a broker, you're getting farmers helping them hedge crops and whatnot?
turns.zh: 很难做到。就像调转泰坦尼克号一样。是啊，完全正确。那你做经纪人的时候，是帮农民对冲作物之类的吗？

turns.en: Or like they were doing marketing and saying, hey, you could trade corn. Like people might say trade crypto or something today. So I would help out some individuals, but more than anything, I was a broker's broker.
turns.zh: 还是说他们做营销，跟人说，嘿，你可以交易玉米。就像今天有人会说交易加密货币那样。所以我会帮一些个人，但更多时候，我是经纪人的经纪人（broker's broker）。

turns.en: So I would help out entire introducing brokers throughout the countryside, you know, feed them the research that I was getting out of Sparks companies, feed them the information I was getting from other brokers.
turns.zh: 所以我会帮全国各地的介绍经纪商（introducing broker），给他们我从 Sparks 公司拿到的研究，给他们我从其他经纪人那里得到的信息。

turns.en: I was kind of a hub of information to help out those guys along the way and ultimately to help out their farmers and cattle ranchers, et cetera.
turns.zh: 我算是一个信息枢纽，一路帮这些人，最终帮到他们的农民和牧场主等等。

turns.en: Then what happened to Willard? When did he pass? Willard passed in, I think it was 2004. Yes, I think that's right. But he had sold his firm into Revco?
turns.zh: 那后来 Willard 怎么样了？他什么时候去世的？Willard 去世是在，我想是 2004 年。是的，我想没错。但他把他的公司卖给了 Refco 吗？

turns.en: No, Revco was gone by then. Revco had folded into MF Global by then. He had sold the research company Sparks to Informa and since then Informa has sold out to S&P Global.
turns.zh: 不，Refco 那时候已经没了。Refco 那时候已经并入了 MF Global。他把研究公司 Sparks 卖给了 Informa，之后 Informa 又卖给了 S&P Global。

turns.en: So his original research firm starting back in August of 77 is still alive. It's just under a different name. Yeah. But he was way more than research, right?
turns.zh: 所以他最初那家从 77 年 8 月起步的研究公司还活着。只是换了个名字。是啊。但他远不止是做研究的，对吧？

turns.en: He was researched. He was brokerage. He was doing a CTA, trading his own account, cash cotton, like the whole gambit. He was more involved in cattle than he was in crops.
turns.zh: 他做研究。他做经纪。他做 CTA，交易自己的账户，现货棉花，全套都做。他涉入养牛比作物更深。

turns.en: I believe, don't quote me, I believe that before he passed away, he was feeding about 350,000 head of cattle, which would have made him the largest private cattle rancher in the United States at that time.
turns.zh: 我记得，别引用我，我记得他去世之前，育肥了大约 35 万头牛，这会让他在当时成为美国最大的私人牧场主。

turns.en: Trading them, but not owning them. Oh, no, he owned every head that went into his feed yard. 100%. At least that's what I understand. So then you were there doing the brokerage.
turns.zh: 交易它们，但不拥有它们。哦，不，进他育肥场的每一头牛他都拥有。百分之百。至少我是这么理解的。所以那时候你在那儿做经纪。

turns.en: I lost track there. Yeah. And so I left in 2006 and went to Dickon Commodities, worked for John Dickon. Dickon. And in 2000. And they were pure discretionary or they had systematic ways to look at all these grains?
turns.zh: 我有点跟不上了。是的。所以我 2006 年离开，去了 Dickon Commodities，为 John Dickon 工作。Dickon。在 2000 年。他们是纯主观的，还是有系统化的方法来看所有这些谷物？

turns.en: Purely discretionary. All in. Purely discretionary. Yeah, for the most part, yes. And he would ask you guys to push information up to him or something.
turns.zh: 纯主观。全押。纯主观。是的，大部分时候是的。那他会要求你们把信息推送上去给他之类的吗？

turns.en: So I was in charge of lots of different things. It was a small firm. John ran a lean shop and I mean, just honestly handled it with a plume.
turns.zh: 所以我负责很多不同的事。那是家小公司。John 经营得很精简，我是说，坦白讲他一个人当几个人用。

turns.en: It's from John Dickon. That's where I really learned risk management. He is still probably the best risk manager I've ever met in my life. And obviously, if you grow to a billion dollars, you have to be really good at risk management in the ag space.
turns.zh: 就是从 John Dickon 那里，我真正学会了风险管理。他至今可能仍是我这辈子遇到的最好的风险管理者。显然，如果你要做到十亿美元规模，你就必须非常擅长农业领域的风险管理。

turns.en: But no, I would handle everything from trade execution, idea generation, help him with sizing of trades, risk parameters, you know, just jack-of-all-trades really.
turns.zh: 但不，我从交易执行、想法生成，到帮他确定交易规模、风险参数，什么都干，我是说，真的是个多面手。

turns.en: So that's where I really cut my teeth on the trading side, understanding truly I was learning the fundamentals and I had a good grasp of the fundamentals.
turns.zh: 所以那才是我在交易这一侧真正打磨自己的地方，真正理解——我在学基本面，我对基本面有很好的掌握。

turns.en: But taking research and turning it into action, that was a skill that I had not yet developed. And John helped me develop that skill. And I'm forever grateful for the opportunity that he gave me.
turns.zh: 但把研究转化为行动，那是一项我还没培养出来的技能。John 帮我培养了这项技能。我永远感激他给我的这个机会。

turns.en: It's a lot of that because the research is kind of hedged. They kind of be like, not right most, if you're in a research report, you're not usually taking a stand.
turns.zh: 很多时候是因为研究本身有点两头下注。他们会有点像，不十分明确，如果你在一份研究报告里，你通常不会表明立场。

turns.en: I'm like, this is a screaming bun. It's like, well, this could happen. Maybe that could happen. We'll see. It's somewhere in the middle. Right.
turns.zh: 我会说，这是个绝佳买点。他们却像，嗯，这可能发生，也许那也可能发生。我们再看吧。它总在中间某个位置。对。

turns.en: And some of the best research guys I have ever met in my life, they can't trade. The risk is too much where they don't know how to size it or they can't handle the fluctuations and equity that come with trading.
turns.zh: 而且我这辈子遇到过的一些最好的研究员，他们不会交易。风险太大了，他们不知道怎么定规模，或者他们承受不了交易带来的净值波动。

turns.en: There's all kinds of reasons, but at the same time, I've known some really, really good researchers who tend not to be great traders, but at the same time, I know some really great traders who are not very good at research.
turns.zh: 有各种各样的原因，但同时，我认识一些非常非常好的研究员，他们往往不是伟大的交易员，可同时我也认识一些非常伟大的交易员，他们做研究并不在行。

turns.en: So I mean, they don't necessarily go hand in hand. I mean, I know people who are able to do both and do both well, but at the same time, I know people who are able to trade just magnificently and they're really not good researchers.
turns.zh: 所以我是说，这两者不一定形影不离。我是说，我认识能两者兼顾并且都做得很好的人，但同时，我也认识交易得极其出色、但研究做得真不怎么样的人。

turns.en: Let's dig into that for a minute. What exactly we mean by research in the ag space, because a lot of people might have different thoughts if they're thinking of, right, if I'm an analyst for a Wall Street firm and I'm pouring over research reports, that's basically like what their revenues and costs and expenses are.
turns.zh: 我们花一分钟深挖一下。在农业领域我们说的“研究”到底指什么，因为很多人可能有不同的想法，如果他们在想，对，如果我是一家华尔街公司的分析师，我在仔细研读研究报告，那基本上就是他们的收入、成本、费用是什么。

turns.en: So what exactly do we mean by research in the ag space? Well, it all comes down to supply and demand at its core to keep it as simple as possible.
turns.zh: 所以在农业领域我们说的“研究”到底指什么？嗯，归根结底就是供给和需求，尽可能简单地说。

turns.en: You've got worldwide crop production and then you have worldwide demand and balancing those two is what the job of price discovery is. So the larger the production, the more demand that you need to buy, which indicates that the prices need to go lower in order to spur that demand.
turns.zh: 你有全球的作物产量，然后你有全球的需求，把这两者平衡起来就是价格发现（price discovery）的工作。所以产量越大，你需要用更低的价格来刺激出足够的需求。

turns.en: Conversely, when supply is low, prices need to go high to curtail demand. So at its simplest form, that's what it is. On a more detailed level, you're dealing with not just the supply, it's easy when you back it into the US, but when you start looking at a worldwide basis where you're looking at production in China, Ukraine, Russia, North Africa, Middle East, Europe, all the way into the United States, Canada, Mexico, down into South America and South America has become
turns.zh: 反过来，当供给低的时候，价格需要走高来抑制需求。所以最简单的形式就是这样。在更细致的层面上，你要处理的不只是供给——只盯着美国很容易，但当你开始从全球角度看，你要看 China、Ukraine、Russia、北非、中东、Europe，一直到 United States、Canada、Mexico，往下到南美，而南美已经成为

turns.en: obviously a very, very big producer. Brazil is the largest producer of soybeans in the world at this point in time, largest exporter at this point in time.
turns.zh: 显然一个非常非常大的生产地。Brazil 目前是世界上最大的大豆生产国，也是目前最大的出口国。

turns.en: So I mean, there's a whole lot of different pieces that go into the puzzle. So one of the four, go ahead. Just confusing to me, right? It's all public information.
turns.zh: 所以我是说，这个拼图里有很多不同的部分。所以四个之一，你说吧。就是让我有点困惑，对吗？这些都是公开信息。

turns.en: These governments and whatnot are releasing this production, right? Like the USDA here, right? You can look at the USDA production and obviously that's what the market uses as its benchmark.
turns.zh: 这些政府什么的都在发布这些产量数据，对吧？比如这里的 USDA，对吧？你可以看 USDA 的产量，显然那就是市场用来作为基准的东西。

turns.en: But when you're growing a crop, USDA can say, okay, production is X. And then we start looking at weather over the growing season and we either add or subtract from that production potential in the crop.
turns.zh: 但当你在种一季作物时，USDA 可以说，好，产量是 X。然后我们开始看整个生长季的天气，我们要么在这产量潜力上加，要么减。

turns.en: I mean, for the research is projecting as much as it's just reporting or way more than just right if I'm doing research on whatever, I'm just looking at what's actually been published and the research that people are trading on is like, okay, these were the numbers.
turns.zh: 我是说，研究到底是像报道一样去预测，还是远远不止于此？对，如果我在做什么研究，我只是在看已经公布的东西，而人们据以交易的研究是像，好，这些是数字。

turns.en: Here's all these factors where the numbers may go for next season. Correct. You're always projecting out on the supply side and then you're also projecting out on the demand side.
turns.zh: 这是所有可能让下一季数字走向何方的因素。对。你总是在供给侧向外预测，然后你也在需求侧向外预测。

turns.en: So like this summer, the weather was really, really good until about the last 10 days of July in the U.S. And the corn plant pollinates toward the end of July and the beginning of August.
turns.zh: 所以像今年夏天，天气真的非常好，一直到 7 月最后 10 天左右，在美国。而玉米在 7 月底、8 月初授粉。

turns.en: And that is its critical growing period. And we turned off hot and we turned off dry. And more than anything, corn is a cool season grass. So when you give it hot temperatures, it really doesn't do well.
turns.zh: 那是它的关键生长期。然后我们突然转热、转干。而且最重要的是，玉米是一种冷季草（cool season grass）。所以当你给它高温，它真的长不好。

turns.en: So it means on the other hand, they really don't care too much about temperatures. They don't want, you know, you don't want over a hundred or anything like that on an extended basis.
turns.zh: 所以这意味着，另一方面，大豆其实不太在意温度。它们不希望，你知道，你不希望长时间超过一百华氏度之类的。

turns.en: But as long as they get water, they tend to do really well. So you had a combination for corn where it was really hot. It was really dry for about four weeks.
turns.zh: 但只要它们得到水，它们往往长得非常好。所以玉米这边你碰上的组合是，天气真的很热、真的很干，持续了大约四周。

turns.en: And that took the top end off of the crop. And the question was always, how much damage did we do? And so I had my own proprietary model that I used to project out what the yield is going to look like on a nationwide basis and then able to back into, you know, what is exactly the balance sheet look like going forward?
turns.zh: 这就削掉了作物产量的上限。而问题始终是，我们到底造成了多大的损害？所以我有一个我自己的专有模型，用来预测全国范围内的单产会是什么样，然后能够反推出，你知道，未来的供需平衡表到底长什么样。

turns.en: And so you still use outside research or no? I'll use some outside research, but most of my agricultural research is in-house. So you were doing the research you were at?
turns.zh: 所以你还是用外部研究，还是不用？我会用一些外部研究，但我大部分农业研究都是内部做的。所以你是在 Dickens 那儿做研究的？

turns.en: Dickens. Dickens. Yes. Not Dickies. Not the overalls. Dickens. So yeah, finish that story. Dickens to get in your own, hang in your own shingle.
turns.zh: Dickens。Dickens。是的。不是 Dickies。不是那个背带工装裤。是 Dickens。所以 yeah，把那个故事讲完。从 Dickens 到自立门户，挂上你自己的招牌。

turns.en: Well, I mean, so John was always very supportive of me learning to trade because it helped him. And so he allowed me to take on managed accounts, trade my own proprietary account.
turns.zh: 嗯，我是说，John 一直非常支持我学交易，因为这对他也好。所以他允许我接管理账户，交易我自己的自营账户。

turns.en: He was, like I said, he was just very supportive of the entire endeavor. So I have been trading managed accounts since 2000. I didn't start Davis Commodities until 2016, but I've been managing money for other people for 20 years now.
turns.zh: 就像我说的，他对整件事都非常支持。所以我从 2000 年就开始交易管理账户了。我 2016 年才创立 Davis Commodities，但我替别人管钱已经 20 年了。

turns.en: You still have a little bit of hair. 20 years managing people. It's a lot grimmer than it was 20 years ago, I can promise you that. And would he back you?
turns.zh: 你还有点头发。管钱 20 年。我可以向你保证，比 20 年前稀疏多了。那他会给你资金背书吗？

turns.en: Would he be like, here's a prop account, I'll put up the money and you trade it and we'll split the profits? That was exactly the great question, Jeff.
turns.zh: 他会说，给你一个自营账户，我出钱你来交易，我们分利润吗？那正是——问得好，Jeff。

turns.en: That was exactly how he started me out. And then I made enough money to where I didn't need his anymore. And so I started just trading my prop account alongside a couple of other managed accounts.
turns.zh: 那正是他一开始给我的方式。然后我赚的钱足够多，不再需要他的了。所以我就开始交易我自己的自营账户，同时管另外几个管理账户。

turns.en: And then eventually, and with, I did absolutely no marketing at all. And it was just kind of a word of mouth. But eventually I had too many managed accounts to not be registered with the NFA as a commodity trading advisor.
turns.zh: 然后最终，我完全没做任何营销。就是靠口碑。但最终我的管理账户多到不得不去 NFA 注册成为商品交易顾问（CTA）。

turns.en: So thus Davis Commodities was born. How many months did it take you to come up with that name? I'm original in a lot of ways, but coming up with the name, no, that was not original at all.
turns.zh: 于是 Davis Commodities 就诞生了。你想出这个名字花了几个月？我在很多方面都挺有原创性，但想名字，不，这一点原创都没有。

turns.en: That was as boring as it could be. Right most hedge fund, they're going to go like read a Greek dictionary, find some weird name that means hunter, gatherer, maybe when the egg's based.
turns.zh: 那真是无聊到极点。对，大多数对冲基金会去翻一本希腊语词典，找个奇怪的名字，意思是猎人、采集者，也许跟蛋有关。

turns.en: You're just like, nope, I'm going to trade commodities and my last name is Davis, boom. That's exactly right. If you could go back 20 years and tell that young you trading, right, do you think you were good right off the bat or do you like, would you shake him a bit?
turns.zh: 你就是，不，我要交易商品，我姓 Davis，搞定。完全正确。如果你能回到 20 年前，告诉那个正在交易的年轻的你，对，你觉得自己一开始就很棒吗，还是你会 shake 他一下？

turns.en: What are you doing, you idiot? What were some of the things you did right in the beginning that you now know are stupid? Well, like every new trader, I think every new trader, at least every trader I've ever met at the beginning, you trade too big and the volatility shakes you out of really good positions.
turns.zh: 你在干什么，你这白痴？你一开始做对、但现在知道很蠢的事情有哪些？嗯，就像每个新交易员一样，我觉得每个新交易员，至少我遇到过的每个交易员，一开始你都交易得太大，波动会把你从真正好的仓位里震出去。

turns.en: That would be the one thing that I would tell me. You had the trade right and the result ended wrong. Yes, simply because the drawdown was too big.
turns.zh: 那就是我会告诉自己的一件事。你交易方向对了，结果却错了。是的，仅仅因为回撤太大了。

turns.en: The structure of the trade was incorrect and that was one of the things that forced me to learn. In the end, it probably wasn't a, I mean, don't be wrong, it was a bad thing, but it wasn't a bad thing to lose a little bit of money on the front end simply because it allowed me to learn how to structure trades so I don't get shaken out and I'm there when the move actually happens.
turns.zh: 交易的结构不对，那是逼我去学习的东西之一。到最后，它可能不是——我是说，别误会，它是件坏事，但前期亏一点钱并不是坏事，仅仅因为它让我学会了如何构建交易，这样我就不会被震出去，而当行情真正发生时我就在场。

turns.en: And that's even more important today than it was 20 years ago. I feel like that's invaluable. I almost don't trust someone who hasn't lost earlier in their career, right, because it's probably coming for everyone and if they haven't, it's something they don't know yet that's built into their model or whatnot that might show up at a future date.
turns.zh: 而这在今天比 20 年前更重要。我觉得那是无价的。我几乎不信任一个在职业生涯早期没亏过钱的人，对，因为它对每个人可能都会来，如果他们还没遇到，那就是他们模型里之类还没意识到的某个东西，可能在未来某天冒出来。

turns.en: There's no doubt about that. I mean, you do have anomalies out there of guys who really never lost money and I'd love to know how they figured out their risk parameters that early on, but they're few and far between.
turns.zh: 毫无疑问。我是说，确实有一些反常的家伙真的从没亏过钱，我很想知道他们那么早是怎么搞定自己的风险参数的，但那种人凤毛麟角。

turns.en: You know, it's kind of funny that, you know, so I started in 2006 and I lost money in 2006. I made money every year thereafter through 2015 and I was feeling a little bulletproof.
turns.zh: 你知道，有点好笑，所以我是 2006 年入行的，2006 年我亏了钱。之后每一年我都赚钱，一直到 2015 年，我开始觉得自己有点刀枪不入了。

turns.en: And in 2016, we had had a, we were a tight carry-in of soybeans. There were problems with the Argentine soybean crop and I said, there's no way soybeans can go down.
turns.zh: 到了 2016 年，我们的大豆结转库存很紧。Argentine 大豆作物有问题，我说，大豆不可能跌。

turns.en: There's no way without a massive record yield in the U.S. and weather turned perfect. We found out how big of a soybean crop we can grow here when weather is right.
turns.zh: 除非美国出现创纪录的巨大单产，否则不可能跌，结果天气转好了。我们发现当天气对的时候，我们这儿能种出多大一季大豆。

turns.en: And yeah, I mean, I jokingly said that the market can have my soybean position when they pry it from my cold dead fingers. Well, they almost did, yeah.
turns.zh: 而且是啊，我是说，我开玩笑说，市场想要我的大豆仓位，除非从我冰冷僵硬的手指里把它掰走。结果他们差点真掰走了，是啊。

turns.en: So it was a good recentering for me. I mean, I was still old enough to know better, but still young enough in the business to where I was going to make those kinds of mistakes.
turns.zh: 所以那对我来说是一次很好的重新校准。我是说，我年纪已经够大该懂事了，但在这个行业里还够年轻，所以我还是会犯那种错误。

turns.en: And it forced me into reexamining all of my risk parameters and turning my guidelines into roles and I really took it. It took that big loss for me to step in and say, okay, what works and what doesn't and push forward with what does, how to keep the risk in control, but still deliver solid returns on the other side.
turns.zh: 它逼我重新审视我所有的风险参数，把我的指引变成规则，我真的接受了。是那次大的亏损让我踏进来说，好，什么有效、什么无效，然后带着有效的东西往前走，怎么把风险控制住，同时在另一端交付稳健的回报。

turns.en: You have two strategies, right? I have three now. Three. Three. Yes. That was a test you passed. All right. You have three strategies. So I know you mainly from the ag grain strategy, but talk, let's take them one in order wherever you want to start.
turns.zh: 你有两个策略，对吧？我现在有三个。三个。三个。是的。那是你通过的一次测试。好。你有三个策略。所以我主要是从农产品谷物策略认识你的，但说说吧，我们一个一个来，你想从哪儿开始都行。

turns.en: Sure. I mean, we'll start with the one that I, that I, my original one, which is called Plutus. There's your, you know, great name that, that, yeah, all right.
turns.zh: 好。我是说，我们就从我最初那个开始吧，它叫 Plutus。这就是你的，你知道，“好名字”，那个，yeah，好吧。

turns.en: So it kind of makes it stand out as my ag program. So that trades corn, soybeans, soybean products, wheat, cattle, feeder cattle. That's it.
turns.zh: 所以它算是我的农产品项目的招牌。它交易玉米、大豆、大豆产品、小麦、牛、育肥牛（feeder cattle）。就这些。

turns.en: It is a completely discretionary. You should call it the Memphis program. It's like everyone in Memphis knows those things. I almost call it the singing river because where I go to the lake, they call that portion of the, of the Tennessee river, the singing river.
turns.zh: 它是完全主观的。你应该叫它 Memphis 项目。就像 Memphis 人人都知道这些东西。我差点叫它 Singing River，因为我去的那个湖，他们把 Tennessee 河的那一段叫 Singing River。

turns.en: It goes back to Native American times, but anyway, anyway, so it's completely discretionary, fundamentally based program. I am not a short-term trader.
turns.zh: 那要追溯到美洲原住民时代，但总之，总之，所以它是完全主观的、基于基本面的项目。我不是短线交易员。

turns.en: My trades last as little as a month. Usually that's kind of the bare minimum of, of what I'm in a trade for and can last as much as six months to multiple years.
turns.zh: 我的交易最短也持续一个月。那通常算是我在一个交易里的最低限度，最长可以持续到六个月乃至好几年。

turns.en: The reason why I say six months is just simply because we have the Northern Hemisphere growing and then we have the Southern Hemisphere growing six months later.
turns.zh: 我说六个月的原因很简单，就是我们北半球在种植，然后南半球在六个月后种植。

turns.en: And so your, your balance sheets can completely shift in six months from surplus to, you know, tight stocks in the opposite at the same time.
turns.zh: 所以你的供需平衡表可以在六个月内从过剩完全转向，你知道，紧张库存，反之亦然。

turns.en: And when you say balance sheets, you mean supply of each of those commodities. Yeah. Correct. Correct. And sometimes you can see a shift in demand as well, but yes, it's mainly the, the supply driven, you know, Northern Hemisphere, Southern Hemisphere dichotomy.
turns.zh: 你说的供需平衡表，是指每一种商品的供给。是的。对。对。有时候你也能看到需求的转变，但是的，它主要是那个供给驱动的、你知道，北半球、南半球的二元格局。

turns.en: And so what's that look like? You come in, I guess you kind of always have a trade on, but say you come in no position, you're, you look at each separately or is it a mosaic of like they go together in certain ways?
turns.zh: 那是什么样子的？你进来，我猜你基本上总是有仓位，但假设你进来时没有仓位，你是分别看每一种，还是它们像一幅拼图，以某些方式关联在一起？

turns.en: Well, it's a great question because most times they trade independently, but if for some reason we really hurt the corn crop and we didn't hurt the soybean crop, corn can trade at a high enough price to where soybeans kind of get pulled into their gravitational area, their gravitational field.
turns.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题，因为大多数时候它们独立交易，但如果因为某种原因我们严重损害了玉米作物、却没损害大豆作物，玉米可以交易到足够高的价格，把大豆也拉进它的引力场。

turns.en: And they don't go nearly as low as what they should fundamentally. But to your point, you can't look at everything in a vacuum. You have to see the big picture and then pull back into the pieces.
turns.zh: 于是大豆跌不到它按基本面本该跌到的那么低。但就像你说的，你不能孤立地看每一样东西。你必须看到全局，然后再收回到各个部分。

turns.en: And then for the pieces, you're, you're just going to, okay, corn, here's what, here's all the reports. Here's what I'm projecting. Here's what my model says, go take us through what that looks like to get each trade on, what the sizing looks like, the risk.
turns.zh: 然后对于各个部分，你就是，好，玉米，这是所有的报告。这是我预测的。这是我的模型说的，去——带我们走一遍，那是什么样子，怎么建立每一笔交易，规模是什么样，风险是什么样。

turns.en: So I mean, like right now, I am negative prices on both corn and soybeans for different reasons and kind of ironically for corn, I told you earlier that yes, we did do some damage to the US corn crop this year.
turns.zh: 所以我是说，就像现在，我对玉米和大豆都持看跌（negative）态度，原因不同，而且有点讽刺的是，对玉米来说，我早先告诉过你，是的，我们今年确实对美国玉米作物造成了一些损害。

turns.en: It's not terrible. It's not an abject failure. It's just not quite what we call a trend yield. So trend goes up about, you know, 1.6, 1.7 bushels every year, better seed technology, better planting technology, better use of fertilizers, all kinds of stuff goes into it.
turns.zh: 它不算糟。它不是彻底的失败。它只是不太是我们所说的趋势单产（trend yield）。所以趋势每年大约上升，你知道，1.6、1.7 蒲式耳，更好的种子技术、更好的种植技术、更好的化肥使用，各种因素都在里面。

turns.en: So we're going to come in a little bit underneath trend, simply because we did do a little bit of damage to the crop. The problem with corn right now is that it has a demand this year.
turns.zh: 所以我们会略低于趋势线，仅仅因为我们确实给作物造成了一点损害。玉米现在的问题是，它今年的需求。

turns.en: So USDA has exports coming down. Last year was record large corn exports to the war, you know, from the United States. And USDA has got it coming down about 120 million bushels year over year.
turns.zh: 所以 USDA 把出口往下调。去年是创纪录的巨大玉米出口，从 United States 到全世界。而 USDA 把它下调了大约 1.2 亿蒲式耳，同比。

turns.en: Well, we're only two months into the crop year and export commitments are down 400 million bushels already. Once you get to the first quarter of the crop year, which is September, October, November, you can gain some of that back by doing bigger exports through the rest of the year.
turns.zh: 可是我们才进入作物年度两个月，出口承诺量就已经少了 4 亿蒲式耳。一旦你到了作物年度的第一季度，也就是 9 月、10 月、11 月，你可以通过在余下时间做更大的出口把一部分补回来。

turns.en: It's just tough to do. So I'm a little bit of a demand bear on corn right now. The wild card is obviously China. And we've heard a lot of President Trump speaking about China and they're going to buy 25 million tons of soybeans and $17 billion worth of another ag.
turns.zh: 只是很难做到。所以我现在对玉米有点算是需求上的空头。那个变数显然是 China。我们听到很多 Trump 总统在讲 China，说他们要买 2500 万吨大豆和 170 亿美元的其他农产品。

turns.en: The sources that I have in China are basically saying that if prices get right, China will buy ag out of the U.S. But the prices have to get right.
turns.zh: 我在 China 的消息源基本上是说，如果价格合适，China 会从美国买农产品。但价格必须合适。

turns.en: And right now we're just not competitive into the Chinese market for corn. So it may make sense at some point in the future if prices get low enough.
turns.zh: 而现在我们在玉米上进入中国市场就是没有竞争力。所以在未来某个时点，如果价格足够低，也许说得通。

turns.en: Because of today, it really doesn't make sense. Where else is that export business going? Oh, we export basically everywhere around the world.
turns.zh: 因为就今天而言，它真的说不通。那这些出口业务还流向哪里？哦，我们基本上向全世界出口。

turns.en: You know, EU, Middle East, North Africa, Japan, a lot of Southeast Asia buys U.S. corn. So I mean, it's a pretty wide swath. Mexico is a huge importer of U.S. corn, mainly because it comes in by rail.
turns.zh: 你知道，EU、中东、北非、Japan，很多东南亚国家买美国玉米。所以我是说，覆盖面相当广。Mexico 是美国玉米的巨大进口国，主要是因为它靠铁路运输进来。

turns.en: And with the geography of Mexico being that mountain range right dead in the center, it's kind of hard to transport stuff over that mountain range.
turns.zh: 而由于 Mexico 的地形是那条山脉正好横在正中央，把东西翻越那条山脉运过去相当难。

turns.en: So it's much easier to bring it in through Texas via rail. And as you said before, all this corn is 99%, 95% used just for feeding cattle or feeding livestock in general.
turns.zh: 所以通过 Texas 用铁路运进来要容易得多。而且就像你之前说的，所有这些玉米有 99%、95% 只是用来喂牛或者一般来说喂牲畜。

turns.en: The corn that we trade is 100% used for feed. Feed and ethanol, that's a misnomer. Ethanol obviously with the 2006 bill for the renewable fuel, that's been a huge portion of the demand growth in U.S. corn.
turns.zh: 我们交易的玉米是 100% 用于饲料。饲料和乙醇，那是个误解。乙醇显然随着 2006 年那项可再生燃料法案，一直是美国玉米需求增长的巨大一部分。

turns.en: But you ever see that going away? New administration, new? No, not only do I not see it going away, they've kind of doubled down on the renewable fuel standard, not so much on the ethanol side, but on the renewable diesel and biodiesel.
turns.zh: 但你有没有看到它消失的可能？新政府，新的？不，我不仅没看到它消失，他们还在某种程度上加倍押注了可再生燃料标准，不是在乙醇这一侧那么多，而是在可再生柴油（renewable diesel）和生物柴油（biodiesel）。

turns.en: So made out of basically any fat oil, but the way that they've structured it, it is favored to use domestic supplies of soybean oil, halos, and then imported, especially canola oil from Canada.
turns.zh: 所以基本上用任何油脂（fat oil）来做，但他们构建的方式是，它偏向于使用国产的大豆油、牛脂（tallow），然后是进口的、尤其是来自 Canada 的芥花籽油（canola oil）。

turns.en: Those all qualify. All right, so corn. So anyway, you're saying you put that whole puzzle together, you think prices are right? The demand side is what's causing you pause, so then that builds into a short position?
turns.zh: 这些都合格。好，那么玉米。总之，你是说你把整个拼图拼起来，你觉得价格是对的？是需求侧让你犹豫，所以那就构建成一个空头仓位？

turns.en: Correct. And then that's just outright futures, there's options in there, what does that look like? 90% of my trade, 85% is options. I like to define what the risk is going to look like.
turns.zh: 对。那然后那就是纯粹的期货吗，里面有期权吗，那是什么样子？我 90% 的交易，85% 是期权。我喜欢界定风险会是什么样子。

turns.en: Now I will wrap futures with options. If the volatility is high, I don't want to own high volatility, I'm not a vol trader, but I don't want to own high volatility options, because I've seen what happens when you start moving the market lower in corn, soybeans, wheat, the volatility just implodes.
turns.zh: 现在我会用期权来包裹期货。如果波动率高，我不想持有高波动率，我不是波动率交易员，但我不想持有高波动率的期权，因为我见过当玉米、大豆、小麦市场开始走低时会发生什么，波动率就直接崩塌。

turns.en: So owning options and a high volatility regime is a good way to not necessarily lose money, you just make less. And so I like to use a futures versus options strategy to where I'm able to take some of that volatility back out of the market.
turns.zh: 所以在高波动率的环境下持有期权，是一种不一定亏钱、但你只是赚得更少的好办法。所以我喜欢用期货对期权（futures versus options）的策略，让我能够从市场里把一部分波动率拿回来。

turns.en: So what else in this model we know? So your risk control is just that option premium, or you have other risk controls on time then? For sure, a lot of traders employ a lot of leverage in their futures strategies, which is very, very easy to do in futures as you well know.
turns.zh: 所以这个模型里我们还知道些什么？那么你的风险控制就是那笔期权费，还是你在时间上有其他风险控制？当然，很多交易员在他们的期货策略里用很高的杠杆，这在期货里非常非常容易做到，你很了解。

turns.en: And I limit my exposure to 150% of the net asset value of the accounts that I'm trading. Which still some people's heads might explode like 150%, what?
turns.zh: 而我把我的敞口限制在我所交易账户净值的 150%。这仍然会让有些人的脑袋爆炸，150%，什么？

turns.en: Well, it's kind of funny because when I go into a position, I never have a 100% of assets under management exposed to any position I have on.
turns.zh: 嗯，这有点好笑，因为我建仓的时候，我从不会让我所管理的资产的 100% 暴露在我持有的任何一个仓位上。

turns.en: The way that it gets to above 100% is simply that the position starts working and at that point, I get up to 125, 130 because it's working and then I have to move the deltas around to get the position back down to 100%.
turns.zh: 它之所以会超过 100%，仅仅是因为仓位开始朝着有利方向走，到那个点，我会涨到 125、130，因为它在走，然后我必须调整 delta，把仓位降回 100%。

turns.en: The reason why I put 150 is sometimes the market just moves really fast in the right direction and it's very difficult to maintain the exact 100 that I really, really want.
turns.zh: 我之所以定 150，是因为有时候市场就是朝正确方向走得很快，很难维持我真正、真正想要的那个精确的 100。

turns.en: So you're looking at deltas there, so you're in this short corn, you're owning puts or whatever. There are 20 deltas, say when you put them on and all of a sudden they're 150, minus 150 delta and you're like, all right, I got to bring these back to 100.
turns.zh: 所以你在那儿看的是 delta，所以你在这个玉米空头里，你持看跌期权（put）之类的。假设你建仓时它们是 20 delta，突然它们变成 150、负 150 delta，你就想，好，我得把这些拉回到 100。

turns.en: Yes. That's exactly right. Yes. That's exactly right. And it's aggregated across every position that I have, so it's a net delta position. Sometimes I'll go long corn, short beans, long beans, short corn, long wheat, short corn and vice versa, but it's always aggregated back out to the net delta and then I don't ever let the leverage of the overall, the gross position get out of hand either.
turns.zh: 是的。完全正确。是的。完全正确。而且它是在我持有的每一个仓位上汇总的，所以它是一个净 delta 仓位。有时候我会做多玉米、做空大豆，做多大豆、做空玉米，做多小麦、做空玉米，反之亦然，但它总是汇总回净 delta，然后我也从不让整体总仓位（gross）的杠杆失控。

turns.en: That's capped at 300%. And then those long shorts aren't a spread trade, you're not trying to trade that basis coming in, you're just trading each of those separately?
turns.zh: 那上限是 300%。那么这些多空不是价差交易（spread trade），你不是想交易那个正在收敛的基差（basis），你只是在分别交易每一个？

turns.en: Well, usually it's a relationship trade. Like right now, soybeans are very expensive on corn and for that reason I'm much shorter soybeans than I am corn, but I'm negative to both, so I'm not going to put on a corn long just to have a spread on.
turns.zh: 嗯，通常它是一个关系交易（relationship trade）。就像现在，大豆相对玉米非常贵，出于这个原因，我做空大豆比做空玉米多得多，但我对两者都看跌，所以我不会仅仅为了持有一个价差就去建一个玉米多头。

turns.en: I just want to focus a little bit more on that, which I think has more downside. Talk to us about soybeans a bit, like you said, I don't think most people in America know what a soybean looks like, right?
turns.zh: 我只是想更关注那个，我认为它下行空间更大。跟我们讲讲大豆，就像你说的，我觉得大多数美国人不知道大豆长什么样，对吧？

turns.en: But especially if they're not sushi eaters, yes, get the head of mommy, but how did this come to be? Has it been here forever? Oh. With like 20 years ago where you're trading beans, sure.
turns.zh: 但尤其是如果他们不吃寿司，是的，毛豆（edamame），但这东西是怎么来的？它一直都在吗？哦。就像 20 年前你在交易大豆那样，当然。

turns.en: Yes. Oh yes. Yeah. Beans really, soybeans really got prevalent in the 70s. It's primarily used as poultry feed. It's an additive in poultry feed, hog feed, and then in dairy cattle.
turns.zh: 是的。哦是的。是啊。大豆，大豆真正盛行起来是在 70 年代。它主要用作家禽饲料。它是家禽饲料、猪饲料里的添加剂，然后是奶牛。

turns.en: We use very little soybean meal in actual beef cattle production. The steak that you eat has almost none in the ration, but soybeans are kind of like crude oil.
turns.zh: 我们在实际的肉牛生产里用很少的豆粕。你吃的牛排，日粮里几乎没有它，但大豆有点像原油。

turns.en: Nobody uses crude oil, right? You use unleaded gas, you use diesel, you use jet fuel, soybeans are the same way. Nobody really uses a soybean.
turns.zh: 没人用原油，对吧？你用无铅汽油，你用柴油，你用航空燃油，大豆是一样的。没人真的用一个“大豆”。

turns.en: A soybean is put into a crushing place, and the feed grade soybeans are handled a little bit differently than the feed grade. Those are dried down.
turns.zh: 大豆被送进一个压榨厂，而饲料级的大豆处理方式略有不同。它们被烘干。

turns.en: You wouldn't even recognize it. They get a little bit bigger than a BB. It's like a big BB. Oh wow. Yeah. They really do get pretty small. But no, the soybeans go into what's called a crushing plant, and from there they actually literally crush the soybean, and you get two products out of it.
turns.zh: 你都认不出来。它们比一颗 BB 弹稍大一点。就像一颗大 BB 弹。哦哇。是啊。它们真的会变得相当小。但不，大豆被送进一个叫压榨厂（crushing plant）的地方，从那儿他们真的字面意义上压榨大豆，你从中得到两种产品。

turns.en: You get soybean meal, which goes into animal feed, and then you get soybean oil, which up until very recently is primarily a food, goes into our food chain, and you can go buy your Snickers and what's on there, soybean oil, all that kind of stuff, goes into salad dressings, just pretty much runs the gamut.
turns.zh: 你得到豆粕（soybean meal），它进动物饲料，然后你得到豆油（soybean oil），直到最近它主要是一种食品，进入我们的食物链，你可以去买你的士力架（Snickers），上面写的是什么，豆油，所有那类东西，进沙拉酱，基本上应有尽有。

turns.en: But so you get basically about 80% of the soybean is meal and 20% is oil, and so you have your balance sheet for the soybean itself, and then you have a balance sheet for the soybean meal, and you have a balance sheet for soybean oil.
turns.zh: 但所以你基本上得到，大豆的大约 80% 是豆粕、20% 是豆油，所以你有大豆本身的供需平衡表，然后你有豆粕的供需平衡表，你有豆油的供需平衡表。

turns.en: So soybeans are a little bit more in-depth than corn is at this time. It's protein. Right? It's protein source. Soybean meal is like... Cheap protein source.
turns.zh: 所以大豆在这个时点比玉米要更深入一些。它是蛋白质。对吧？它是蛋白质来源。豆粕就像……廉价的蛋白质来源。

turns.en: 48% protein. So if I own a bunch of cattle, I own pigs, I'm trying to feed them. This is my cheapest protein source, basically. As a general rule, yes.
turns.zh: 48% 的蛋白质。所以如果我养了一群牛、养了猪，我想喂它们。这基本上是我最便宜的蛋白质来源。作为一般规律，是的。

turns.en: That's correct. Yeah. Absolutely. Right? That's what's interesting to me, like versus corn and wheat, that's just filler, right? What are they doing?
turns.zh: 对。是啊。绝对的。对吧？有意思的是，跟玉米和小麦比，那只是填充物，对吧？它们在干什么？

turns.en: They're not offering any protein. Corn, let's say. Corn has a little bit of protein. Wheat has more protein than corn, but what they found is that when you feed the protein into especially hogs, poultry, even into fish, the conversion rates go up rapidly, and there's an optimized point on that, and I'm not a feed ration guy, so you don't ask me the exact ration.
turns.zh: 它们不提供任何蛋白质。玉米，这么说吧。玉米有一点蛋白质。小麦的蛋白质比玉米多，但他们发现，当你把蛋白质喂进去，尤其是喂猪、家禽，甚至喂鱼，转化率会迅速上升，而且有一个最优点，我不是做饲料配方的，所以你别问我确切的配方。

turns.en: Corn versus meal, I couldn't tell you that, but all I know is that with the current feeding practices, the conversion rates have gone through the roof, and we just feed animals much more efficiently today than we did 50 years ago.
turns.zh: 玉米对豆粕，我说不上来，但我所知道的是，以当前的喂养方式，转化率已经飙升，我们今天喂养动物的效率比 50 年前高得多。

turns.en: But the whole math, like I'll take you to your macro now, like the whole math is the world's doing better, people have more money, they're buying more steak, and they're buying more proteins themselves, right?
turns.zh: 但整个逻辑，就像我要把你带到你的宏观（macro）了，整个逻辑是世界在变得更好，人们有更多钱，他们在买更多牛排，他们自己也在买更多蛋白质，对吧？

turns.en: Steak, chicken, fish, pork, and that needs protein itself, right? That needs to be fed, which is what drives most of the market. That's the whole game.
turns.zh: 牛排、鸡肉、鱼、猪肉，而那本身需要蛋白质，对吧？那需要被喂养，这才是驱动大部分市场的力量。这就是整盘棋。

turns.en: Yes, 100%. And our biggest growth in soybean meal and soybean, and even to some extent corn demand has actually come from some of the poorer countries here over recent years, you know, Middle East, North Africa, typically were very small users of the protein source of soybean meal as well as corn additive.
turns.zh: 是的，百分之百。而且我们在豆粕、大豆、甚至某种程度上玉米需求上最大的增长，其实来自近年一些较穷的国家，你知道，中东、北非，通常是豆粕这种蛋白质来源以及玉米添加剂的很小的用户。

turns.en: They were just feeding it basically whatever they had laying around on the very low level. There are obviously some commercialized farms that were already feeding, but we've seen money growth, we've seen demand growth in all meats worldwide, and that is the driver for the growth of all ag products at this point in time, and it's about two to two-and-a-half percent a year.
turns.zh: 他们基本上就是在很低水平上用手头随便有什么喂什么。显然也有一些已经商业化的农场在喂，但我们看到了货币增长、看到了全世界各种肉类的需求增长，而这才是当前所有农产品增长的驱动力，大约是每年 2% 到 2.5%。

turns.en: And then wasn't there some, was it bean oil was getting smashed last year? When they're palm oil versus bean oil, there's something going on with bean oil?
turns.zh: 那么是不是有一些，去年豆油是不是被打得很惨？当棕榈油（palm oil）对豆油，豆油那边有什么事在发生？

turns.en: Well, bean oil is making it a, no, bean oil has been a very political football. We knew that the government was talking about expanding the use of vegetable oils and animal fats, even used cooking oil to turn into biodiesel and renewable diesel.
turns.zh: 嗯，豆油正在让它成为一个，不，豆油一直是一个非常政治化的橄榄球（政治皮球）。我们知道政府在谈论扩大植物油和动物脂肪的使用，甚至用过的食用油，把它们变成生物柴油和可再生柴油。

turns.en: What we didn't know was the magnitude, and it's funny, you talk to people who should be in the know out of Washington and they didn't know. So bean oil went through this entire process of Lucy holding the football for Charlie Brown for a while.
turns.zh: 我们不知道的是量级，而且好笑的是，你去跟华盛顿那些本该知情的人聊，他们也不知道。所以豆油经历了这整个过程，就像 Lucy 给 Charlie Brown 扶着橄榄球那样，持续了一阵子。

turns.en: Oh, it's going to be great, and then all of a sudden the government would go, we're not ready to do anything about that yet. So they would pull the proverbial football out of the way and soybean oil would crash and then it would come right back.
turns.zh: 哦，这会很棒，然后突然政府会说，我们还没准备好对此做任何事。于是他们会把那枚象征性的橄榄球抽走，豆油就崩，然后又弹回来。

turns.en: Now we know what the mandate is and just suffice to say it's big. We are going to be turning a lot of food into fuel over the next several years.
turns.zh: 现在我们知道这个强制掺混令（mandate）是什么了，只能说它很大。未来几年我们要把大量食物变成燃料。

turns.en: Is that not enough food? It seems dangerous, right? Hey, we need fuel instead of food, don't worry about starving people. Well, you know, without getting into the politics of it, I don't believe that it was necessarily the best decision that we could make.
turns.zh: 那食物不够吗？这看起来危险，对吧？嘿，我们要燃料而不是食物，别管挨饿的人。嗯，你知道，不扯进政治的话，我不认为这必然是我们能做出的最好决定。

turns.en: Fuel makes people unhappy. Hungry makes them downright mad. Yeah, revolting. Yes, that's how you end up with hunger and starvation. That's how you end up with revolution.
turns.zh: 燃料让人不快。饥饿让人真正愤怒。是啊，会造反。是的，那就是你怎么走向饥荒和饿殍。那就是你怎么走向革命。

turns.en: That's how you end up with lots and lots of problems. So look, unfortunately, or fortunately, however you want to look at it, it's not my decision as to what policy looks like.
turns.zh: 那就是你怎么走向一大堆一大堆的问题。所以你看，不幸也好、幸运也罢，随你怎么看，政策长什么样不是我能决定的。

turns.en: My job is simply to say, okay, this is policy, how do I trade this? What is the environment looking like going forward? I don't get the luxury of right and wrong in my work life.
turns.zh: 我的工作只是说，好，这是政策，我怎么交易它？未来的环境看起来是什么样？在我的工作生活里，我没有对错这种奢侈。

turns.en: I can have my own personal opinions about everything, but my work life is based on the reality of where we're sitting today and trying to project where we're going to be tomorrow.
turns.zh: 我可以对每件事有自己的个人观点，但我的工作生活是基于我们今天所处的现实，并试图预测我们明天会到哪儿。

turns.en: So from that standpoint, it does get very interesting that you take your personal beliefs and you set those aside and you just simply trade what is given to you by the government at any point in time, which has made this environment actually very difficult because, as we all know, Trump can be a little off the cuff and you may not know what's coming next.
turns.zh: 所以从那个角度看，把你自己个人的信念放到一边，只去交易政府在任何时点给你的东西，这确实变得非常有意思，而这实际上让这个环境非常艰难，因为众所周知，Trump 可能有点随口就来，你可能不知道下一步是什么。

turns.en: So the political footballs have been pretty rampant of late and will probably be that way for another two years. How do you think about your small shop there in Memphis?
turns.zh: 所以这些政治皮球最近相当泛滥，可能未来两年还会是这样。你怎么看待你在 Memphis 那家小公司？

turns.en: You've got big, huge hedge funds and firms and even car deals and big, huge commercial traders that have every bit of info you have, all the sources, right?
turns.zh: 你有那些巨大、庞大的对冲基金和公司，甚至 Cargill 这种，还有巨大、庞大的商业交易商，他们拥有你有的每一点信息、所有的消息源，对吧？

turns.en: How do you compete with those big guys or do you think of that in that way? It seems like right if I had all the money in the world, I could model all this and it be perfect.
turns.zh: 你怎么跟那些大家伙竞争，或者你会那样想吗？看起来是，对，如果我有世界上所有的钱，我可以把这一切都建模、做到完美。

turns.en: So there's like an art and a science to it, right? It's not just getting access to the numbers. I don't know if there's a question in there, but yeah.
turns.zh: 所以这里面既有艺术也有科学，对吧？不只是拿到那些数字。我不知道这里面有没有问题，但 yeah。

turns.en: No, I'm following what you're saying and it's a good question. And what's interesting is really about 2020, 2021, we saw the funds that I was generally competing against shift in their focus.
turns.zh: 不，我在跟着你说的思路，这是个好问题。有意思的是，大约 2020、2021 年，我们看到我通常在竞争的那些基金转变了它们的关注点。

turns.en: Most of those funds now are more algorithmic based. They're no longer trading the same things that I am, which actually gives me a bit of an edge.
turns.zh: 那些基金现在大多更基于算法。它们不再交易跟我一样的东西，这其实给了我一点优势。

turns.en: I mean, if you go around, I don't know how many different traders you talk to on a daily basis or monthly basis, but how many of them are discretionary traders?
turns.zh: 我是说，如果你四处走走，我不知道你每天或每月跟多少不同的交易员聊，但他们当中有多少是主观交易员？

turns.en: A lot of them. A lot of them. More so now. Yeah. I was just saying that it's kind of like shifted back to, yeah, they were kind of person non-grotto like 10 years ago, like, oh, discretionary, I want to model.
turns.zh: 很多。很多。现在更多了。是啊。我刚才就是说，它有点像是转回来了，yeah，他们十年前有点像是——主观交易是个不受欢迎的人（persona non grata），像，哦，主观的，我要建模。

turns.en: And now the models are like table stakes and I feel like it's shifting back. But yeah, for sure there was a move towards like, ooh, discretionary, no, I want all systematic.
turns.zh: 而现在模型就像是入场筹码（table stakes），我感觉它正在转回来。但 yeah，确实曾经有一阵子风向是，哦，主观的，不，我要全系统化。

turns.en: Right. And so, I mean, to be in the discretionary basket for basically, since I started trading, I think it puts me in a little bit different of a position.
turns.zh: 对。所以我是说，基本上自我开始交易以来就待在主观这个篮子里，我觉得这让我处在一个有点不一样的位置。

turns.en: I don't view most of the hedge funds really as competition because as a general rule, they're either trend-following or they're very short-sighted as far as their trade outlook.
turns.zh: 我并不真把大多数对冲基金当作竞争对手，因为作为一般规律，他们要么是趋势跟踪（trend following），要么就是交易视野非常短视。

turns.en: I'm not looking for the next 15 minutes. I'm not looking for the next 30. I'm not looking for the next day. My trades, like I said, they're longer-lasting, they're big longer-term ideas, not so much.
turns.zh: 我找的不是接下来 15 分钟。我找的不是接下来 30 分钟。我找的不是接下来一天。我的交易，就像我说的，是更持久的，它们是大的长线想法，而不是那么——

turns.en: This is what we're doing today. As a general rule, day-to-day is a random walk. So I really try to focus on that which I can control, which tends to be a little bit longer out.
turns.zh: 这就是我们今天在做的。作为一般规律，逐日的走势是一场随机漫步（random walk）。所以我真的努力聚焦在我能控制的东西上，那往往是更远一些的。

turns.en: But then that puts you kind of opposite the big commodity houses and ... Well, sometimes, and sometimes they're on my side. Or maybe on the same page, yeah.
turns.zh: 但那就把你放在了大型商品行情的对立面……嗯，有时候，有时候他们跟我一边。或者说站在同一页上，是啊。

turns.en: Like currently, the funds, they've had this big story, lots of stories as to why you need to be bullish ag. We've had the Russia Ukraine, the US Iran, a lot of fertilizer comes out through the Strait of Hormuz.
turns.zh: 就像目前，这些基金，他们有过这个大故事、很多故事，讲为什么你需要看多农产品。我们有过 Russia-Ukraine、US-Iran，很多化肥是通过 Strait of Hormuz 运出来的。

turns.en: Their whole story going back to the spring was we're going to run out of fertilizer. Well, that one didn't hold water because most people who needed fertilizer for spring planting already owned the fertilizer.
turns.zh: 他们从春天开始的整个故事就是我们要把化肥用完了。嗯，那个站不住脚，因为大多数需要化肥春播的人早就已经拥有化肥了。

turns.en: So the earliest that would be a problem was the fall. And we haven't really seen a problem out of fertilizer yet in the fall either. The wars were going to cause massive inflation and inflation means buy commodities.
turns.zh: 所以最早会成问题的时候是秋天。而我们在秋天也还没真看到化肥出问题。战争会导致大规模通胀，而通胀意味着买商品。

turns.en: And so they came in and they bought all the commodities. And so far, outside of really a few different commodities, it really hasn't come to light either.
turns.zh: 所以他们进来买了所有的商品。到目前为止，除了真的少数几种商品，它还真的没兑现。

turns.en: So the stories are kind of being picked off one by one. And they're long. I mean, the funds, the big hedge funds, they are really, really long.
turns.zh: 所以这些故事正被一个一个地击落。而且他们是多头。我是说，这些基金、这些大型对冲基金，他们真的、真的做多。

turns.en: Right now, they're wrong. So it's going to take some, they need to help at this point. If you want to get soybeans going sharply higher again, you need a massive weather problem in South America.
turns.zh: 现在他们是错的。所以要花一些，他们需要在这个点上帮忙。如果你想让大豆再次大幅走高，你需要南美出现一个巨大的天气问题。

turns.en: That was the other story, El Nino, this super El Nino. And what people don't understand is that, yes, Super El Nino can be bad for Australia.
turns.zh: 那是另一个故事，El Nino，这个超级 El Nino。而人们不理解的是，是的，超级 El Nino 可能对 Australia 不利。

turns.en: Did not manifest this year. Super El Nino can be bad for Indian weather. This year, they had a very subpar monsoon season. What's interesting is when you get into South America, the El Nino can be beneficial or detrimental.
turns.zh: 今年没有出现。超级 El Nino 可能对 India 的天气不利。今年他们有一个非常低于常年的季风雨季。有意思的是，当你进到南美，El Nino 可能是有利的，也可能是有害的。

turns.en: There's really no clear cut as to whether El Nino is really that bad of a deal for South America. Generally, what happens is the northern portions of Brazil are a little drier than normal.
turns.zh: 对于 El Nino 对南美到底是不是那么糟糕的事，其实没有明确的定论。一般来说，会发生的是 Brazil 的北部地区比正常略干。

turns.en: The southern portions are wetter and that kind of comes close to offsetting each other than usually get a really big crop out of Argentina. So, I mean, this is just, once again, going by tendencies, not, I'm not prognosticating what the weather is going to look like in three months because nobody knows.
turns.zh: 南部地区更湿，而这大致接近相互抵消，然后通常从 Argentina 得到一个很大的作物。所以我是说，这只是，再一次，按倾向性走，不是，我不是在预言三个月后的天气会是什么样，因为没人知道。

turns.en: But this thought process that El Nino equals bad is a wrong thought process. It's a very interesting thing that I've had to manage over the last six months, really.
turns.zh: 但“El Nino 等于糟糕”这个思维过程是一个错误的思维过程。这真的是我在过去六个月里必须管理的一件非常有意思的事。

turns.en: Have you ever go down the path of like, I need my own weather team and weather models and, right, you get some of these big funds and groups that start doing, going down that rabbit hole of like, if I could just get a better handle on the weather, I could really trade this stuff well.
turns.zh: 你有没有走过那条路，像，我需要我自己的天气团队和天气模型，对，你会看到一些大基金和机构开始走那个兔子洞，像，如果我能对天气有更好的把握，我就能把这些东西交易得很好。

turns.en: So, I'm really fortunate. I'm affiliated with a training group called Nesvic Trading Group. They do basically all of my operations for me. So, I don't have to worry about new accounts and compliance and all these kinds of things.
turns.zh: 所以，我非常幸运。我隶属于一个叫 NSVC Trading Group 的交易集团。他们基本上替我做所有的运营。所以我不必操心新账户、合规以及所有这类事情。

turns.en: I basically just come in and trade. The other great service that they provide for me is they have, in my opinion, the greatest agricultural meteorologist in the United States on staff.
turns.zh: 我基本上就是进来交易。他们为我提供的另一项很棒的服务是，在我看来，他们有全美最伟大的农业气象学家在职。

turns.en: And so, I get his weather every day. I'm able to talk to him every day. If I've got a question, he's just immediately right there. And his name's Craig Solberg, and he probably, he is one of the backbones of the operation.
turns.zh: 所以我每天都能拿到他的天气。我每天都能跟他聊。如果我有问题，他就立刻在那儿。他叫 Craig Solberg，他大概，他就是这个运营的支柱之一。

turns.en: I mean, he really keeps me on track as far as what the weather is looking like around the world. And so, no, I don't have to worry about going out and outsourcing that.
turns.zh: 我是说，他真的让我保持在正轨上，知道全世界的天气看起来是什么样。所以，不，我不必操心出去把那个外包。

turns.en: Right. But do you feel like you've seen that other places, right? Of like, people think it kind of seems to me like a red queen race for, right?
turns.zh: 对。但你有没有在别的地方看到过那种情况，对？就像，人们觉得，在我看来它有点像一场红皇后赛跑（red queen race），对吧？

turns.en: You're just always going to be chasing that belief that you can solve the weather. Like, I guess that's the question. Is the weather even solvable?
turns.zh: 你就是永远在追逐那个“你能搞定天气”的信念。就像，我猜这才是问题。天气到底能不能解？

turns.en: Or you just want to have an idea so you're not too far out of bounds one way or the other? That's a great point. A lot of people try to go out three months, six months, and say what the weather's going to look like.
turns.zh: 还是说你只是想有个大致概念，好让你不会往任何一个方向偏得太离谱？这是个很好的点。很多人试图往三个月、六个月去看，说天气会是什么样。

turns.en: I look out 15 days. That's it. That's it. Hard stop. 15 days. Wow. Hard stop. Even though your trades could be months. Correct. 15 days. And if I need to pull the ripcord on a trade because the weather changes, I'm going to pull the ripcord.
turns.zh: 我只看 15 天。就这样。就这样。硬性上限。15 天。哇。硬性上限。即便你的交易可能持续好几个月。对。15 天。如果我需要因为天气变化而拉一个交易的开伞索，我就会拉。

turns.en: And I did over the summer. I had to flip and go long because the weather was detrimental to corn. And so I did for a bit. And then I was like, okay, now we've discounted that weather problem.
turns.zh: 而且我在夏天就这么做了。我不得不翻转去做多，因为天气对玉米不利。所以我做了一阵子。然后我就想，好，现在我们已经把那个天气问题贴现进去了。

turns.en: And now the risks are shifting back the other way. So, you know, when the weather market's going on, you have to pay attention. But it is not, it's a rarity that you really get a massive weather problem.
turns.zh: 而现在风险正在往另一个方向转。所以你知道，当天气行情在进行时，你必须留意。但它不是，真正出现一个巨大天气问题是很少见的。

turns.en: And the last one we had in the U.S. was 2012. I'm talking about a big weather problem. Was that partly technology also? Like we have more ways to handle the bad weather.
turns.zh: 我们在美国碰到的上一次是 2012 年。我说的是一个大天气问题。那部分也是因为技术吗？就像我们有更多办法去应对坏天气。

turns.en: Like you have a tractor that can go through the mud better. You have water resistant fertilizer that doesn't get washed away. Things like that.
turns.zh: 就像你有一台能更好地穿过泥地的拖拉机。你有抗水的化肥，不会被冲走。那类东西。

turns.en: So, the hybrids are a little bit better at dealing with drought. It's rare that you really have, I mean, don't get me wrong, you can lose a little bit of yield because of nitrogen leaching with too much rain.
turns.zh: 所以，那些杂交品种（hybrid）在应对干旱上要好一点。你真的很难得有，我是说，别误会，你可能因为雨水太多导致氮流失（nitrogen leaching）而损失一点单产。

turns.en: But that just means that you're going to lose 5, 10, 15 bushels from an individual field, not necessarily the national average. Where we really get into trouble is drought.
turns.zh: 但那只是意味着你会在单独一块地里损失 5、10、15 蒲式耳，而不一定是全国平均。我们真正陷入麻烦的是干旱。

turns.en: And, you know, the last big drought we had was 2012. I think it's been 14 growing seasons since then. Which is weird, you seem like you read about drought on the, you see drought on the news all the time.
turns.zh: 而且你知道，我们上一次大干旱是 2012 年。我想那之后已经过了 14 个生长季。这挺奇怪的，你好像总在新闻上看到干旱。

turns.en: This area's in new drought. This one's in new drought. Sure. And that's localized. Exactly. I mean, like we had an ongoing drought down in the southern plains.
turns.zh: 这个地区在闹干旱。那个地区在闹干旱。当然。那是局部的。对。我是说，就像我们南部平原（southern plains）一直有一场持续的干旱。

turns.en: And that'll go down a different rabbit hole, but that's why your beef prices are so high because they had to liquidate the herd because there was no hay.
turns.zh: 那会走到另一个兔子洞，但那就是为什么你的牛肉价格这么高，因为他们不得不清群（liquidate the herd），因为没有干草。

turns.en: There's no grass to feed these cattle. So, but yes, you do get localized droughts, but when you're starting to talk about, we're going from North Dakota down through Kansas, eastern Colorado, all the way east to, you know, a lesser extent, but, you know, all the way over to the Carolinas, Virginia.
turns.zh: 没有草来喂这些牛。所以，但是的，你确实会有局部干旱，但当你开始说，我们要从 North Dakota 往下穿过 Kansas、eastern Colorado，一路往东到，你知道，某种较小程度上，一路到 Carolinas、Virginia。

turns.en: Yeah. And you're talking about a mass swath of the U.S. and you can have a localized area that has a problem. But getting a widespread drought, like I said, that hasn't happened since 2012.
turns.zh: 是啊。你说的是美国一大片地带，你可以有一个局部地区出问题。但出现一场大范围干旱，就像我说的，那自 2012 年以来还没发生过。

turns.en: And that was detrimental. I mean, I remember walking through cornfields that year and it was early August. And the corn was dead. It was just dead.
turns.zh: 而那一次是有害的。我是说，我记得那年我走过玉米地，那是 8 月初。玉米都死了。就是死了。

turns.en: Couldn't help it, couldn't hurt it, couldn't do anything to it at that point. But, you know, that was just kind of the way it was. Do you still do that?
turns.zh: 帮不了它，也伤不了它，到那个点你什么都做不了。但你知道，那大概就是当时的样子。你现在还那样做吗？

turns.en: Or is that part of your process, right? Like a lot of these Chicago guys used to go on crop tours and send back pictures, right, to the trade desk.
turns.zh: 还是那是你流程的一部分，对吧？就像很多这些 Chicago 的家伙以前会去做作物巡查（crop tour），把照片发回来，对吧，发给交易台。

turns.en: Like, look at, they're like picking up dirt and taking a picture and sending it. Yeah. I am very fortunate in that I don't have to do that anymore.
turns.zh: 就像，看，他们像在抓起泥土拍张照发出去。是啊。我很幸运，我现在不必那样做了。

turns.en: That was, that was nine days of getting cut up because I don't know if you ever walked through a cornfield, but those leaves are actually pretty sharp.
turns.zh: 那是九天被割得遍体鳞伤，因为我不知道你有没有走过玉米地，但那些叶子其实相当锋利。

turns.en: You know, so you're going to be like 100 paper cuts on your arms. And, you know, it just wasn't a very comfortable process. And in the end, the number of samples that we got, what really wasn't high enough to give us a clear depiction of what the crop is going to be.
turns.zh: 你知道，所以你胳膊上会有大概 100 道纸割伤。而且你知道，那真不是一个很舒服的过程。到最后，我们拿到的样本数量真的不够高，不足以给我们一个作物会什么样的清晰图景。

turns.en: So now I'm, I'm fortunate that I don't have to do that. I've, I've got a really good yield model that takes into account all the weather, planting dates, emergent states.
turns.zh: 所以现在我很幸运，不必那么做了。我有一个很好的单产模型，它把所有天气、种植日期、出苗状况都考虑进去。

turns.en: You know, it goes through, you know, when the crop is, is going through its reproductive cycle. And ironically, I'm getting basically just as good or better data than I got from walking through a field.
turns.zh: 你知道，它会走一遍，你知道，作物什么时候在经历它的生殖周期。而讽刺的是，我得到的数据基本上跟我走过一块地得到的数据一样好、甚至更好。

turns.en: Yeah, it seems, seems old fashioned. So you're telling me it is old fashioned. Yeah. There's still firms that do it. I mean, you've got some of the big commercials that, that still do massive crop tours.
turns.zh: 是啊，这听起来老派。所以你告诉我它确实是老派的。是啊。还有一些公司会那样做。我是说，你有一些大的商业商，他们仍然做大规模的作物巡查。

turns.en: And those are beneficial. But when you got two guys in a truck trying to get enough counts, get enough empirical data to really move the needle, you just, Well, I'm like, where, and now a day is where you got to do one in Australia.
turns.zh: 而那些是有益的。但当你只有两个人开着卡车，试图拿到足够的计数、足够的经验数据来真正撬动指针时，你就是——嗯，我是说，现在你在哪儿，如今你还得去 Australia 做一次。

turns.en: You got to go down to Brazil. You got, right? I actually, I actually did crop tours in Brazil back in the day. Ooh. So what does that look like versus 20 years ago?
turns.zh: 你还得下去 Brazil。你还得，对吧？我实际上，我当年真的在 Brazil 做过作物巡查。哦。所以那跟 20 年前比是什么样子？

turns.en: Were you, was South America and Australia a thing, but not nearly as big of a thing? Brazil had already been on the upswing. They weren't, they weren't, they hadn't overtaken the U.S. as the largest producer of soybeans, but they were big.
turns.zh: 那时候，南美和 Australia 是不是一回事，但远没有那么重要？Brazil 那时就已经在上行。他们还没有、还没有超过美国成为最大的大豆生产国，但他们已经很大了。

turns.en: And first of all, Brazil is absolutely beautiful. But what's interesting is that, you know, in the United States, a big field is 50 or 75 acres.
turns.zh: 而且首先，Brazil 是绝对美丽的。但有意思的是，你知道，在美国，一块大地是 50 或 75 英亩。

turns.en: And in Brazil, it's hundreds of acres big. I mean, it's just this massive open area in spots. And yeah, I mean, their fields are just on a different level from the U.S.
turns.zh: 而在 Brazil，是几百英亩大。我是说，就是一些地方那种巨大的开阔地带。而且是啊，我是说，他们的田地就跟美国不是一个量级。

turns.en: But is that, is that harder nowadays? Like the stuff you have to do today, you got to know about all these global markets, right? You were talking before I got a price, the Northern Hemisphere, I got a price, Southern Hemisphere, there's never a rest, right?
turns.zh: 但那在今天是不是更难？就像你今天必须做的那些事，你得了解所有这些全球市场，对吧？你之前在讲，我拿到一个价格，北半球，我拿到一个价格，南半球，永远没有休息，对吧？

turns.en: It used to be grain, I remember the grain traders like kind of took off, right? Like, oh, I just threw crop season, then it's quiet period for a while.
turns.zh: 以前是谷物，我记得那些谷物交易员有点像收工了，对吧？就像，哦，我刚过了作物季，然后是一阵安静期。

turns.en: Right, back before Brazil and Argentina became the big producers that they are now. Yes, absolutely. I mean, you would plant your corn crop, your bean crop, we'd go through the summer, and then basically you just trained in demand for the rest of the year until you got into the next planting season in April.
turns.zh: 对，那是在 Brazil 和 Argentina 成为如今这样的大生产者之前。是的，绝对的。我是说，你会种下你的玉米作物、你的大豆作物，我们度过夏天，然后基本上你就在余下的时间里交易需求，直到你进入 4 月的下一个种植季。

turns.en: That is completely changed. And it actually, in some ways, it's harder, but it's also a lot more fun for me. You know, when you're just tracking demand all the time, okay, well, that's great.
turns.zh: 那已经完全改变了。而且实际上在某些方面它更难，但对我来说也有趣得多。你知道，当你只是一直在追踪需求时，好，嗯，那很好。

turns.en: I can track demand. But I like having multiple inputs. I don't know why, but my brain for some reason likes that. All right, take us through the other two strategies.
turns.zh: 我可以追踪需求。但我喜欢有多个输入。我不知道为什么，但我的大脑不知怎么就喜欢那样。好，带我们走一遍另外两个策略。

turns.en: Sure, I've got a global macro program that basically trains everything that the Plutus program doesn't. So I trade metals, energies, currencies, interest rates, stock indices.
turns.zh: 好，我有一个全球宏观（global macro）项目，基本上交易 Plutus 项目不交易的所有东西。所以我交易金属、能源、货币、利率、股票指数。

turns.en: So it basically trades everything else. And it's interesting that the macro program grew out of the Plutus program. And the main reason is, as I alluded to earlier, you know, it was these big macro stories that cause people to buy agricultural commodities.
turns.zh: 所以它基本上交易其他所有东西。而且有意思的是，这个宏观项目是从 Plutus 项目里长出来的。主要原因是，正如我早先提到的，你知道，正是这些大的宏观故事促使人们去买农业商品。

turns.en: And I needed to understand what was going on in the macro world so that I could better forecast what was going to happen to the ag world. Well, then I started trading for myself as most of these things happen.
turns.zh: 而我需要理解宏观世界里在发生什么，这样我才能更好地预测农业世界会发生什么。嗯，然后我就开始为自己交易，就像大多数这类事情的演变那样。

turns.en: And I found that I'm pretty good at it. So I continued trading the macro and then a few years ago, I started that program. And it is the same kind of methodology as the agricultural program as the fundamental inputs obviously are a little bit different.
turns.zh: 我发现自己挺擅长这个。所以我继续交易宏观，然后几年前，我启动了那个项目。它跟农业项目是同一种方法论，只是基本面输入显然有点不一样。

turns.en: You know, there's not necessarily a supply and demand balance sheet that you can do for the U.S. economy. But you get the point that it's all longer term.
turns.zh: 你知道，你不一定能给美国经济做一张供需平衡表。但你懂那个意思，它全都是长线的。

turns.en: It's all big theme, not necessarily trend following at all. But definitely I'm looking for mispriced assets against what I see as the fundamentals of what is ongoing in the economy.
turns.zh: 它全是大主题，完全不一定是趋势跟踪。但我绝对是在寻找那些相对于我所看到的经济基本面而被错误定价的资产。

turns.en: And then going forward, I've got the Atlas program and the Atlas program just spun up and it trades a whole lot more like my personal account does.
turns.zh: 然后往前看，我有一个 Atlas 项目，Atlas 项目刚刚启动，它的交易方式更像我自己的个人账户。

turns.en: So I've been trading my own money in that program since 2016. And yeah, I just spun it out to investors, I believe in July. So it's a brand new program.
turns.zh: 所以我从 2016 年起就用自己的钱在那个项目里交易。而且 yeah，我刚把它推给投资者，我记得是 7 月。所以它是一个全新的项目。

turns.en: But once again, it's got a track record going back to 2016. Nice. And so that's more sometimes it's heavy grains, sometimes heavy macro like goes back and forth.
turns.zh: 但再一次，它有一段能追溯到 2016 年的业绩记录。不错。所以那个更多是，有时候重仓谷物，有时候重仓宏观，来回切换？

turns.en: It has both. It's kind of a blend between the two programs. It is a riskier program. You know, the rules that I have for the Plutus program for the macro program, they are not the same rules that I have for Atlas.
turns.zh: 它两者都有。它算是两个项目之间的一种混合。它是一个风险更高的项目。你知道，我给 Plutus 项目、给宏观项目定的那些规则，跟我给 Atlas 定的规则不一样。

turns.en: It takes a little bit more risk, a little bit more leverage. Like as an example, margin to equity in my Plutus program is usually around 5%.
turns.zh: 它承担多一点风险、多一点杠杆。举个例子，我的 Plutus 项目里，保证金对净值（margin to equity）通常在 5% 左右。

turns.en: Macro program is usually a little bit beneath that. And then the Atlas program stays underneath 10% margin to equity as a general rule. It can go above briefly from time to time, but it's generally sub 10%.
turns.zh: 宏观项目通常略低于那个。然后 Atlas 项目作为一般规律保持在 10% 保证金对净值以下。它偶尔会短暂超过，但一般在 10% 以下。

turns.en: So it's almost, let's call it double the risk. And still all three of those, which I'll answer my own question. Like what, I'm an investor. Why do I want a discretionary ag trader?
turns.zh: 所以那几乎是，我们就叫它两倍的风险。而三个都是这样，这个我自己来回答。就像，什么，我是一个投资者。我为什么想要一个主观农产品交易员？

turns.en: Like what's the logic for why this should be in a portfolio? That's a diversification. I mean, you're heavy in stocks, you're heavy in bonds.
turns.zh: 这背后的逻辑是什么，为什么它应该在一个组合里？那是分散化（diversification）。我是说，你重仓股票、重仓债券。

turns.en: You want something that has no correlation to what you're in. You know, you want to have some diversification. And it was kind of funny. I was at a conference last week for the daily dirt nap.
turns.zh: 你想要某个跟你所持东西没有相关性的东西。你知道，你想要一些分散化。而且有点好笑。我上周在 Chicago 参加了一个会，是为那个 daily dirt 之类的。

turns.en: And I thought, I thought, I was like, I saw you there. But in Chicago, you were in a conference after the conference I saw you. Yeah, I was in a conference after the conference.
turns.zh: 而且我想，我想，我像是，我在那儿看到你了。但在 Chicago，你是在会后的一个会上，我看到你了。是啊，我是在会后的那个会上。

turns.en: It's been kind of a conference heavy couple of weeks. But no, and one of the speakers there, he ran the math on it. And this sounds crazy. But you should have a third of your assets in these diversified portfolio.
turns.zh: 这几周算是会议密集的几周。但不，那儿有一位演讲者，他把这笔账算了一遍。这听起来很疯狂。但你应该把你分散化组合里的三分之一资产放在

turns.en: Kind of the diversification, diversification stuff like commodities. That's what we're raising me. That's what we talk about every week here on the derivative.
turns.zh: 这种分散化、分散化的东西里，比如商品。这就是我们在讲的。这就是我们每周在 The Derivative 上谈的。

turns.en: Well, I mean, most people are like, okay, 5%, 10% needs to go into alternative investments. And the math that he ran showed clearly it's a third in alternative investments.
turns.zh: 嗯，我是说，大多数人会想，好，5%、10% 需要放进另类投资（alternative investments）。而他算的那笔账清楚地显示，是三分之一放进另类投资。

turns.en: Which I answered before. Yeah, that it's only 5% margin equity would make me right. If I'm building the portfolio like, hey, actually that third only needs to be 5% of your cash.
turns.zh: 这个我之前回答过。是啊，只有 5% 保证金对净值这一点会让我觉得对。如果我在构建这个组合，像，嘿，其实那三分之一只需要是你现金的 5%。
